contradiction_resolution: No claim-level contradiction: contradicts_claim_ids is empty, and FND-0067 does not oppose CONJ-0001, THM-0001–THM-0007, OBS-0001, or RED-0001. It is compatible with THM-0005 (c(6)=5, so n=6 needs residual geometry beyond published CKgP), with the packet C66-GEO-Z bottleneck (balanced tetragonal splitting, W_5 failure locus Z, reduced-support open not to be called closed), and with corroborated sibling FND-0052 (balanced reduced-support relative linear system is an open piece of the failure locus, not a closed pure-codimension-4 subvariety of M_{6,6}). Independent checks. (1) Closedness criterion: a subset A of a topological space X is not closed iff cl(A)\A is nonempty; for A=Z^{bal} subset M_{6,6} one must therefore exhibit or otherwise establish a point of cl(Z^{bal})\Z^{bal}. (2) Location in Z\Z^{bal}: the CE evaluation-failure condition is the vanishing of H^0(C, omega_C tensor W_5^vee(Gamma)) (equivalently O_C(Gamma) isomorphic to W_5 tensor omega_C^{-1} on the balanced f=5 summand, SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 / packet FND-0063), hence Z is cut out by a determinantal/Fitting condition and is closed in the ambient moduli; with Z closed and Z^{bal} subset Z one has cl(Z^{bal}) subset Z, so any missing limit point lies in Z\Z^{bal}. Mere existence of some point of Z\Z^{bal} on a different component does not prove non-closedness of Z^{bal}; the point must lie in the closure. (3) Insufficiency of openness-plus-example: upper semicontinuity of cohomology for vector bundles on P^1 makes more-unbalanced splitting types closed conditions, so the balanced locus B^{bal} (F=O(4)oplus O(5) for g=6) is open in the tetragonal Hurwitz/moduli presentation; base-point-freeness is likewise open. SRC-0004 §10 constructs open substacks of smooth tetragonal curves and distinct marked points and records that the splitting type of F enters evaluation independence (Lemma 10.6, Remark 10.7). Openness of balancedness/bpf plus one balanced example therefore yields only that B^{bal} (and any relatively open Z^{bal}=Z cap B^{bal}) is nonempty and open in a suitable ambient—it does not by itself produce a limit point outside Z^{bal}, nor prove properness inside an irreducible component of a closed Z. Alternative legitimate proofs (dimension comparison dim cl(Z^{bal})>dim Z^{bal}; nonempty proper open in an irreducible closed set, using Zariski density) still establish existence of such a closure point and are covered by the finding’s ‘or otherwise establish’ clause. Distinct from FND-0052 (geometric assertion that the balanced reduced-support piece is open/not closed pure of codimension 4, with Gysin requiring a closed stratified embedding after h^0 and splitting-type stratification): FND-0067 is the proof-obligation obstruction blocking fallacious shortcuts to that conclusion, not a restatement of the geometric fact. Distinct from FND-0064 (finite etale S_6-torsor over the reduced-support open) and FND-0058/FND-0060 (dimension/stabilizer gaps for the balanced stack). Merge target: none. Promote from candidate to corroborated; evidence_class upgraded from adversarial_review to primary_source on independent verification of the closed-set criterion, closedness of the evaluation-failure locus, and the insufficiency of openness-plus-example without a boundary witness in Z\Z^{bal}.
